settings.headline: A farm, a tannery and a wallow
settings.subtitle: Cadwallow Park is a fictional city park, opened in 1889 on a farm and an old tannery site around a marshy hollow the farmers called the Cad Wallow. It is run by the city's Parks and Recreation Department, with help from the Friends of Cadwallow Park.

settings.headline: How it became a park
settings.body:
In 1887 the city bought the Harlan farm and the closed tannery on Tanner's Run for $41,000, after a campaign by the newspaper for "a lung for the city". The marshy hollow at the center was dug out into a lake in 1889 and kept its old name.

The Works Department built the boathouse in 1928 and the stone overlook in 1936. The Elm Walk was planted in 1898 and mostly lost by 1970; three of its elms survive. Today the park has 10.6 miles of trail and about two million visits a year.
settings.note: Cadwallow Park, its city and everyone named on this site are invented for a Raytha example. Phone numbers use the 555 range.
